title: Wind-Driven Wildfires Rake Southern California, Burning Homes and Forcing Thousands to Flee
snippet: Fierce Santa Ana winds fueled a rapid surge of wildfires across Southern California, charring thousands of acres, destroying homes in Orange County, and displacing thousands of residents.
content:
SAN JUAN CAPISTRANO, Calif. — A series of explosive, wind-driven wildfires erupted across Southern California, razing homes in Orange County and forcing more than 16,000 residents to evacuate as fierce Santa Ana winds lashed the region.

The fast-moving Norte Fire ignited around noon near residential neighborhoods bordering San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano. Driven by gusty winds and rugged terrain, the blaze rapidly devoured hundreds of acres, damaging or destroying at least six homes and sending thick smoke over Interstate 5.

Orange County Bears the Brunt

As of Saturday morning, the Norte Fire had burned 570 acres and was just 5% contained. Firefighters faced challenging conditions throughout the night as embers blew across dry brush, creating constant risks of new ignitions.

"A majority of the fire has been knocked down. However, we still have some homes that have been impacted here, and as you can see, the wind is still blowing pretty strong," Orange County Fire Authority spokesperson Steve Concialdi said.

Sheriff's deputies went door to door executing mandatory evacuation orders covering roughly 4,600 homes. Nearby schools dismissed students early and canceled after-school programs. Two firefighters suffered significant injuries while defending structures and were reported to be in stable condition at local hospitals.

Representative Mike Levin, whose family was among those forced to evacuate their San Juan Capistrano home, commended first responders for preventing further destruction and noted that the "year-round wildfire season" has effectively become the region's new normal.

Multiple Blazes Across the Southland

The Norte Fire is one of several blazes sparked since Santa Ana wind conditions heightened late Thursday. In Los Angeles County, the 150-acre Bryson Fire in Malibu threatened more than 100 structures and triggered hundreds of evacuations before firefighters achieved 52% containment.

To the south, the Henderson Fire burned more than 3,000 acres near Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton in San Diego County. Although the fire forced temporary closures along Interstate 5 due to heavy smoke, military officials confirmed no personnel or facilities were directly threatened.

To prevent power lines from sparking additional blazes in the volatile conditions, regional utilities temporarily shut off electricity to tens of thousands of customers across Southern California. Fire crews remain deployed across multiple fronts as red flag conditions linger into the weekend.
